# Guided panel
The guided panel is the default interface for the AN/PRC-117G.
It provides the controls needed for normal radio operation while leaving advanced settings on [bold]AUTO[/bold].
By default, AUTO uses:
- FH waveform - MED output power - squelch 3 - the wearer's callsign
The display shows the radio's current state, while the banner below it reports problems that need attention.
Advanced functions such as output power, waveforms, fixed station callsigns, direct frequencies, the search receiver, and operator techniques are available through the [textlink="expert faceplate" link="AU14CommsANPRCExpert"].
## Opening the panel
Wear the radio, then alt-click it, or right-click it and select [bold]Open Radio Panel[/bold].
Only trained operators can open the panel. See [textlink="the AN/PRC-117G" link="AU14CommsANPRC"] for roles that begin with radio training.
The first time the panel is opened, a short briefing appears.
- [bold]GOT IT[/bold] closes the briefing. - [bold]? HELP[/bold] opens it again and provides access to this guide. - [bold]VIEW[/bold] switches between the guided panel and expert faceplate.
The radio remembers the last interface used.
## Display
The display provides the radio's most important status information.
### Working net
The display shows:
- working memory - frequency - loaded net
The [bold]TALK[/bold] line indicates whether [color=#a4885c]:r[/color] can currently transmit.
### Security
The display shows the current waveform and encryption state.
Possible states are:
- [bold]SECURE[/bold] - [bold]NOT SECURE[/bold] - [bold]IN CLEAR[/bold]
### Connection and relay
[bold]SIG[/bold] shows the quality of the radio's connection to its working net.
[bold]RELAY[/bold] shows:
- how many nets the radio is relaying - the current relay range
If the display reads [bold]NOT RELAYING[/bold], the radio is not providing combat-net coverage to nearby headsets.
Common causes include:
- the radio is switched off - the radio is not being worn - the wearer does not have radio training
Check the banner for the specific problem.
## Status banner
The banner below the display reports the next problem preventing normal operation.
Problems are generally shown in the order they should be corrected, such as:
- missing battery - radio switched off - radio not worn - no nets loaded - no valid fill card
When possible, the banner includes a button that corrects the problem directly.
A green banner indicates that the radio is ready for normal operation.
## NETS
The NETS tab manages the radio's memories.
The AN/PRC can contain up to four memory slots.
Each memory shows its contents and whether it is currently being used for transmission or relay coverage.
### Standard nets
[bold]LOAD STANDARD NETS[/bold], or [bold]TURN ON AND LOAD STANDARD NETS[/bold], performs the standard setup.
It:
- switches the radio on - loads available squad and command nets - selects the squad net as the working memory
Existing manually configured memories are not overwritten.
The button only appears while one or more standard nets are missing.
### Memory controls
- [bold]USE[/bold] selects a memory as the working net and marks it [bold]ON AIR[/bold]. - [bold]EDIT[/bold] opens that memory's configuration. - [bold]+ ADD MEMORY[/bold] creates a new empty memory.
Inside the memory editor:
- [bold]Pick a net[/bold] selects the net stored in the memory. - [bold][YOUR SQUAD][/bold] marks the operator's squad net. - [bold][STANDARD][/bold] marks recommended nets. - [bold][IN MEMORY][/bold] marks nets already loaded elsewhere in the radio. - [bold][INTERCEPT][/bold] marks enemy nets resolved by the search receiver. - [bold]Rename[/bold] changes the memory label, up to eight characters. - [bold]EMPTY IT[/bold] clears the memory without removing its slot. - [bold]DELETE MEMORY[/bold] removes the memory slot after confirmation. - [bold]DONE[/bold] closes the editor.
Memory labels are visible only to the operator.
Every friendly combat net loaded into memory is relayed to nearby headsets, regardless of which memory is ON AIR.
A radio can therefore transmit on one net while continuing to relay others.
Direct frequencies are configured through the [textlink="expert faceplate" link="AU14CommsANPRCExpert"].
## LOG
The LOG tab stores the last [bold]50[/bold] radio messages handled by the set.
The newest entries appear first.
The log includes received and transmitted traffic.
Available controls include:
- search by sender or message text - [bold]INTERCEPTS[/bold] - show only intercepted enemy traffic - [bold]ALL NETS[/bold] - cycle through nets represented in the log - [bold]PRINT LOG[/bold] - print the full log - [bold]PRINT INTERCEPTS[/bold] - print only intercepted traffic
Printed logs are placed directly into the operator's hand.
The radio must be worn or staked down before it can print.
A badge on the LOG tab shows how many entries arrived while another tab was open.
## SECURITY
The SECURITY tab displays the radio's encryption state and installed fill card.
Possible states include:
- [bold]ENCRYPTED[/bold] - the installed fill card is current and secured traffic is encrypted - [bold]NOT ENCRYPTED[/bold] - no valid fill card is installed - [bold]FILL SUPERSEDED[/bold] - the installed fill card became outdated after a recrypto - [bold]IN THE CLEAR (PT)[/bold] - the radio is transmitting in plain-text mode
If no valid fill is loaded, use a current COMSEC fill card on the radio.
If the fill is superseded, replace it or receive a new key through over-the-air rekeying.
If the radio is in PT, use [bold]RETURN TO AUTO[/bold] from SETTINGS to restore the normal FH configuration.
### Fill actions
The following actions require confirmation.
- [bold]ZEROIZE[/bold] - eject the active fill card into the operator's hand - [bold]DESTROY FILL[/bold] - destroy the installed fill card - [bold]ORDER RECRYPTO[/bold] - replace the faction's current encryption key and invalidate existing fill cards
ORDER RECRYPTO requires command authority.
ZEROIZE or DESTROY FILL can be used to prevent an installed key from being captured.
## SETTINGS
The SETTINGS tab shows the radio's current operating configuration.
### Operating mode
[bold]HOW THE SET IS RUNNING[/bold] displays [bold]AUTO[/bold] while the radio is using the guided panel's standard settings.
Changes made through the expert faceplate are listed here.
These can include:
- output power - waveform - squelch - fixed station callsign - burst transmission - power save - priority watch - EMCON - retransmission bridge - active search
### Return to auto
[bold]RETURN TO AUTO[/bold] appears whenever the radio is outside the guided panel's standard configuration.
It restores the normal automatic settings and stops an active search.
It does [bold]not[/bold] remove:
- loaded memories - installed fill card
Use RETURN TO AUTO when a radio has been left in an unfamiliar configuration.
For example, a radio left in EMCON cannot transmit or provide relay coverage.
### Monitor
[bold]MONITOR[/bold] listens to every loaded net simultaneously.
While MONITOR is active:
- all loaded nets can be received - the radio becomes receive-only - [color=#a4885c]:r[/color] cannot transmit
### Scan
[bold]SCAN[/bold] listens to every loaded net.
When a loaded net receives traffic, the radio moves ON AIR to that memory.
It remains selected until another loaded net receives traffic or the operator changes it manually.
### Station
[bold]STATION[/bold] shows the callsign currently used by the radio.
Additional controls include:
- [bold]OPEN NET DIRECTORY[/bold] - show callsigns currently assigned to friendly stations - [bold]PHONE[/bold] - open the field-telephone directory
See [textlink="the AN/PRC-117G" link="AU14CommsANPRC"] for field-phone operation.
## Expert faceplate
The guided panel provides everything required for normal radio operation.
The [textlink="expert faceplate" link="AU14CommsANPRCExpert"] provides additional control when needed.
Advanced functions include:
- changing output power - changing waveform - setting a fixed station callsign - entering direct frequencies - enabling power save - enabling EMCON - using priority watch - bridging nets from a staked radio - sending encryption keys over the air - searching for unknown radio nets - locating active jammers
These functions are optional and are not required for basic AN/PRC operation.
